Run a command in a workspace of its own, with an identity of its own

## Usage

```console
coder run [flags] --template <template> [-- command...]
```

## Description

```console
Run a command as a workload. The workload gets its own identity, sponsored by you. It can do nothing in Coder unless you give it scopes, and it never receives your credentials. The command's output is streamed and its exit code returned.

The workload gets a workspace of its own, which its identity owns and shares with you. The workspace is made from the template for this one command, claiming one that was built ahead of time when the template keeps such workspaces, and deleted when the command is over.
  - Run a command and see who it is:

     $ coder run --template agents -- coder identity

  - Let a workload read templates, and nothing else:

     $ coder run --template agents --scope template:read -- coder templates list

  - Keep the workspace afterwards, to look around in it:

     $ coder run --template agents --keep --name fix-1 -- make test

  - Work in a workload's workspace with a terminal:

     $ coder run --template agents -it -- sh

  - List your running workloads:

     $ coder run --list

  - List all of them, with what became of each:

     $ coder run --all

  - Remove a workload, and its workspace with it:

     $ coder run --remove fix-1
```

## Options

### --template

| Property | Value               |
|----------|---------------------|
| Type     | <code>string</code> |

The template the workload's workspace is made from. The workload's identity owns the workspace and shares it with you.

### --preset

| Property | Value               |
|----------|---------------------|
| Type     | <code>string</code> |

The preset of the template to use. A workspace that was built ahead of time for the preset is claimed when there is one.

### --name

| Property | Value               |
|----------|---------------------|
| Type     | <code>string</code> |

A name for the workload. Its workspace is named like it.

### --scope

| Property | Value                     |
|----------|---------------------------|
| Type     | <code>string-array</code> |

A permission the workload may use, as an API token scope such as workspace:read. Repeat it for several. Without any, the workload can do nothing in Coder.

### --keep

| Property | Value             |
|----------|-------------------|
| Type     | <code>bool</code> |

Keep the workspace when the command is over. It stays as it is, and you can enter it. Removing the workload removes it.

### -i, --interactive

| Property | Value             |
|----------|-------------------|
| Type     | <code>bool</code> |

Keep the command's input open. Use it with --tty, as -it.

### -t, --tty

| Property | Value             |
|----------|-------------------|
| Type     | <code>bool</code> |

Give the command a terminal and attach to it. Use it with --interactive, as -it.

### -d, --detach

| Property | Value             |
|----------|-------------------|
| Type     | <code>bool</code> |

Start the workload and print its name instead of following its output.

### -l, --list

| Property | Value             |
|----------|-------------------|
| Type     | <code>bool</code> |

List your running workloads instead of running one.

### -a, --all

| Property | Value             |
|----------|-------------------|
| Type     | <code>bool</code> |

List your workloads, including the most recent ones that are over.

### --logs

| Property | Value               |
|----------|---------------------|
| Type     | <code>string</code> |

Print the output of a workload, by name or identity, instead of running one. A running workload is followed until it ends. For one that is over, the end of its output was kept.

### --remove

| Property | Value               |
|----------|---------------------|
| Type     | <code>string</code> |

Remove the named workload, and its workspace, instead of running one.
